newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russian cosmonauts look well, seen by reporters.
newsitem.headline: Russian cosmonauts look well, seen by reporters.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts who returned to earth from the Mir space station on Thursday looked tired but well.
A Reuter correspondent saw Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin after their Soyuz spacecraft landed in the steppe of Kazakhstan.

The pair left the capsule smiling broadly. Tsibliyev, who had developed stress-induced heart trouble after an accident on June 25, said he felt "happy to be back on earth". He looked more active than Lazutkin, who was resting more.

The cosmonauts, obviously very thirsty, drank water, and then doctors started extensive medical tests. Chief mission doctor Igor Goncharov said Tsibliyev's condition, including his heart and pulse rate, were satisfactory.
